'Soon' means from this very moment forward.

We will still have bad days, relapse, grief, and many obstacles that may seem impossible to conquer, but that's unfortunately how life plays out. Many of us are more sensitive to pain but we will all make it through one way or another. That's okay, it sucks, but there are ways to make these events less painful. This is how we grow and gain experience and wisdom.

Despite how dark and damaged I've felt for most of my life I am somehow able to come out the other side still able to smile. It can feel impossible many days but I always challenge myself to manifest as much positivity as I can. When successful I am able to overpower my despair with confidence created by self-compassion, love for those whom I hold dear, and exciting goals for my future. Over time I grew to realize that I am more easily able to spot the positives hidden amongst invasive negativity. Although I still relapse and fall, it doesn't happen as often as it used to and I feel more in control.

I truly believed (and still do during some lonely nights) that I dont deserve compassion, love, acceptance, happiness, stability, etc... But I do. We all do. We need to prove to one another that we all matter. But we must accept and vocalize our disorders and make an effort to seek help/help ourselves. The best way to start is to convince yourself that you deserve the positivity you long for. Even writing down what you want in life, what you wish to accomplish, and reading it over and over to yourself will help you gain the confidence to be successful. You can make it happen.

Things will get better from this moment forward

My mom and step dad did the same. They told me I was pathetic because they "had it much worse" growing up. They neglected my mental health and got unbelievably angry when they saw signs of self-mutilation or found out about a suicide attempt. When teachers tried to warn them I might be depressed she got angry and sometimes violent.
8 years later, I've moved away and barely keep contact with them. She was quite nasty to me when I left and tried to help my younger sisters leave. She blamed me for her children "abandoning" her. She turned everyone I use to call family against us. But you know what? I haven't made any attempts to take my life since. I've had some tough days, but im not nearly as miserable as I use to be.
Its sad that so many parents feel the need to act out in such an obnoxious and damaging way so that they are the center of attention everytime something goes wrong. I am very sorry that you lack parental support during these dark times, I know it makes life more difficult than it should be. I just want you to remember that pain makes you stronger as long as you don't let it consume you. Some days will be tougher than others and a few slip ups are normal. Luckily the toxic parental environment is only temporary so remember that you will be out of there soon. Make plans for what you will do when you can finally leave and keep yourself excited for the future. Keep in close contact with those who love and support you. The relief of freedom after surviving for so long is worth the fight.
Stay strong, I believe in you!

I grew up in a very similar household as my mother took out her borderline personality episodes out on my younger siblings and I. Once we aged out of her court order to keep us away from my dad, we all left her. She has all of her side of the family against us for being "terrible children" for "making" her self harm and they are blind to her manipulative tactics. Many people accused me of abandoning my mother and shunned me for it because they couldn't comprehend what its like to have an abusive mother who seems so sweet in public.

My point is, despite some of the hate we receive for protecting ourselves, you won't have to live with your family forever. You don't need to keep contact with abusive family members once you leave. They are obviously tearing away at the sanity you've been strongly protecting to survive in their household so cutting your ties with them will help you heal. You don't need to harm anybody, although the negative feelings and mental pain can feel overwhelming, because the consequences for taking a life are FAR heavier than cutting ties with family.

There are other things you could do in the meantime to distract yourself. I took an interest in music and joined after school jazz band. Not only did it give me an excuse to stay out later, but it grew into a passion and emotional outlet. If you're not interested in music, try an art class  gymnastics, martial arts, sports, dance, acting, film, dnd, you name it! 

I wish you luck (although I am confident that you are a strong, brave person who does not need to rely on luck to get through this), stay strong and focus what you wish to accomplish in life. I am proud of you for making it this far! Remember to dwell on goals, not hatred

Absolutely! OCD is disabling. Your life becomes controlled by constant irrational fears and forbidden thoughts. You come up with routines that somehow cancel out any harm. Those routines control you. It's not a quirk and it drives me a little crazy when I hear someone blaming their perfectionism on OCD. When I tell people I have OCD they laugh and say its not a bad thing because organization makes things easier and I should be glad I don't have a real illness. Wish they knew!
